question: Which of the following is the full form of ASCII?

options.text: American Standard Code for Information Interchange
Analytical Scientific Code for Information Interchange
Asian Standard Code for Information Interchange
Analytical Standard Code for Intermitted Information

solution:
The correct answer is __**American Standard Code for Information Interchange.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ASCII stands for **American Standard Code for Information Interchange.**__
 
• It's a standard data-transmission code used by smaller and less powerful computers to represent textual data (letters, numbers, and punctuation marks) as well as non-input-device commands (control characters).
 
• Like other coding systems, it turns data into **standardised digital formats** that let computers communicate with one another and process and store data more efficiently.
 
• The ASCII code was created for teletypewriters but has now found widespread use in personal computers.
 
• Seven-digit binary integers, or numbers made up of multiple sequences of** 0s and 1s**, are used in the standard ASCII coding.
 
• Because there are 128 different possible combinations of seven 0s and 1s, the code can represent **128 different characters.**
 
• A lowercase "p" is represented by the binary sequence 1110000, while an uppercase "P" is represented by the binary sequence 1010000.
 
• The seven information bits plus a **parity bit **(used for error-checking purposes or to represent special symbols) in ASCII code are usually placed in an eight-bit field.
